0.headline: NLC India plans ₹1.5 lakh crore capex push by 2032, targets 31 GW power capacity: CMD
0.heading: NLC India plans ₹1.5 lakh crore capex push by 2032, targets 31 GW power capacity: CMD
0.intro: NLC India will build a 3,200 MW pithead thermal power plant in Odisha worth Rs 35,000 crore and pumped storage projects totalling 2.25 GW. It is also developing domestic critical mineral resources, including vanadium and titanium and pursuing rare earth extraction from fly ash.
0.body:
The renewable energy subsidiary of NLC India is targeting a stock market listing in the current financial year after filing draft IPO documents on November 18. In an interview with Moneycontrol, state-run NLC India chairman and managing director Prasanna Kumar Acharya said the company is yet to finalise the valuation of the renewable energy subsidiary, NLC India Renewables Ltd (NIRL).
NLC India plans to increase its operational renewable energy capacity nearly ninefold to more than 16GW by 2032 from 1,783.96 MW currently, as it looks to supply round-the-clock green power to customers, including data centres. It plans to invest close to Rs 1.5 lakh crore over this period, with more than half earmarked for renewable energy projects, Acharya said.

The expansion will extend beyond renewables. NLC India is targeting an increase in thermal power capacity from around 6.6 GW currently to close to 15 GW by 2032. It also aims to raise mining capacity from around 50 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) to 122 MTPA, including around 8 MTPA of critical minerals. The company is also exploring overseas mining opportunities and pursuing a nuclear power project in partnership with NPCIL.

Edited excerpts:

Your renewable energy arm has filed its DRHP. What is the timeline for its listing, and have you arrived at a valuation?

We are targeting to list it in this financial year itself. We filed the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) on November 18. Valuation and other aspects are being discussed and have not been finalised yet.

What are NLC India's expansion and diversification plans up to 2032, and what investment will they entail?

We revisited our 2032 corporate plan last month and now our focus is on diversification and strengthening conventional thermal power generation. We are targeting close to 15 GW of thermal capacity and more than 16 GW of renewable capacity by 2032.

Our mining capacity is also expected to increase from around 50 MTPA to 122 MTPA, including close to 8 MTPA of critical minerals. The total investment requirement is close to ₹1.5 lakh crore, of which more than 50% will go towards renewable energy projects.

Which projects will drive the expansion in thermal power capacity?

We are trying to put up a fourth unit at Ghatampur in Uttar Pradesh, where our three existing units have a combined capacity of 1,980 MW. At Talabira in Odisha, three units are already there, and we are in the process of tendering one more unit.

We are also planning a greenfield pithead thermal power plant of around 4x800 MW (3,200 MW) near our Machhakata and Patrapara South coal blocks. We have received discom confirmations for power offtake and now we are exploring the joint venture route.

We have also formed a JV with NALCO for a 1,100 MW plant near Machhakata, which will supply power to NALCO's expansion project. In Rajasthan, we have signed a JV agreement for a 2x125 MW project and are preparing to float the tender.

Beyond coal mining and power generation, what are NLC India's plans for diversification into critical minerals, rare earths and other businesses?

We have secured two critical mineral blocks in Chhattisgarh containing phosphorite and limestone, with estimated reserves of around 20 million tonnes and 600 million tonnes, respectively. In Telangana, two blocks contain more than 50 million tonnes of vanadium, over 80 million tonnes of titanium and more than 150 million tonnes of alumina-bearing material. Exploration is underway, and it will take around four and a half to five years to begin mining and processing the Telangana minerals. We will need technology partners for beneficiation.

We have also awarded a contract for a pilot project to extract rare earth elements from Neyveli fly ash, which is expected to be ready by October-November 2027. After observing its performance for 3-4 months, we will decide on commercial-scale development. We have signed MoUs with IREL (India) Ltd for rare earth mining and processing, subject to allocation of the block.

Separately, we have signed an MoU with the Odisha government for beach sand mining.

Besides, at Neyveli, our first overburden-to-sand plant, with a capacity of 4 lakh tonnes per annum, has started selling sand. We are planning two more plants, with capacities of 10 lakh tonnes and 20 lakh tonnes per annum.

How have your coal gasification and energy storage projects progressed?

We have signed an MoU with the Odisha government for a coal gasification project using coal from the Machhakata mines. The feasibility report is under preparation. Once it is ready, we will take the project forward. The government’s viability gap funding (VGF) scheme is also applicable, and we are looking to avail of support under it.

On energy storage, the Odisha government has allocated a 750 MW pumped storage project site to us. The feasibility report has been prepared and accepted, and we are now preparing the detailed project report (DPR). We expect to begin tendering and other activities within the next one and a half years.

We have also identified two pumped storage projects in Tamil Nadu with a combined capacity of around 1.5 GW. Their feasibility reports have been prepared by the state government, and our proposal is under active consideration.

NLC India is evaluating overseas critical mineral assets. What kinds of acquisitions are you considering?

We are primarily looking at copper and gold mining assets in Australia and Chile. We are interested in operational mines that already have beneficiation facilities and offer scope for capacity expansion, rather than greenfield assets that require development from scratch. We are in discussions with 2-3 companies in Australia and have signed a non-disclosure agreement with one of them. Our team has also visited Chile, and we have engaged a consultant to evaluate potential assets.

How have NLC India's plans to foray into nuclear power progressed?

We have signed an MoU with Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) and are now working towards signing the JV agreement and forming the joint venture company within this financial year. NPCIL has identified 3-4 states and is narrowing them down to two before finalising a site. We are discussing two units of close to 700 MW each, with a combined capacity of around 1,400 MW.

1.headline: IIFCL IPO: Govt to part sale stake, company to issue fresh shares
1.heading: IIFCL IPO: Govt to part sale stake, company to issue fresh shares
1.intro: The Cabinet had earlier this year approved the IPO and listing of India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL), and the work is on to file a draft paper with market regulator Sebi for approval.
1.body:
The government is looking to part sale its equity shareholding in IIFCL along with a fresh issue of shares by the company in the initial public offering (IPO), which is likely by the end of the current fiscal year, an official said.

The Cabinet had earlier this year approved the IPO and listing of India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL), and the work is on to file a draft paper with market regulator Sebi for approval.

Without disclosing the quantum of stake dilution, the official said that while the government will reduce its stake by an offer for sale, IFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital in the IPO.

Set up in 2006, IIFCL is a wholly-owned government company providing long-term finances to viable infrastructure projects and is registered as a non-deposit taking non-banking finance company with the RBI.

As of March 31, 2026, IIFCL's gross sanctions stood at over Rs 3.64 lakh crore to about 890 projects under direct lending, takeout finance and refinance, credit enhancement, InVIT and bonds. Cumulative disbursements under these schemes stood at over Rs 1.89 lakh crore.

The proceeds from the government stake sale in IIFCL will add to the government's disinvestment kitty. In the current fiscal year, the disinvestment proceeds stand at Rs 55,757 crore so far.

2.headline: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO allotment tomorrow; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar
2.heading: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO allotment tomorrow; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar
2.intro: The allotment of Mahanadi Coalfields' initial public offering (IPO) is scheduled to be finalised on November 25, with investors able to check their share allocation through the registrar, KFin Technologies, or the stock exchanges.
2.body:
The allotment of Mahanadi Coalfields' initial public offering (IPO) is scheduled to be finalised on November 25, with investors able to check their share allocation through the registrar, KFin Technologies, or the stock exchanges.

The Rs 8,981.12-crore IPO received an overall subscription of 1.52 times by the close of bidding on November 23, according to NSE data. The issue received bids for approximately 74.87 crore shares against 49.31 crore shares on offer.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) drove the demand, subscribing to their reserved portion 4.95 times. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 66 percent, while the retail investor portion received 46 percent subscription. The employee and Coal India shareholder categories were subscribed 22 percent and 56 percent, respectively.

In the grey market, the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO premium had fallen sharply by the end of November 23. InvestorGain's last recorded figure was zero, compared with around 1 percent on the morning of November 23.

The grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee listing gains. It can fluctuate depending on market conditions and demand for the issue.

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO allotment status: How to check

Investors can check their allotment status online once the basis of allotment is finalised on November 25.

Check allotment status on KFin Technologies

Step 1. Visit the KFin Technologies IPO allotment website at https://ipostatus.kfintech.com/
Step 2. Select Mahanadi Coalfields from the list of issues, once available.
Step 3. Choose an identification option, such as PAN, application number or DP/client ID.
Step 4. Enter the required details and submit.
Step 5. Your allotment status will be displayed on the screen.

Check allotment status on BSE

1. Visit the BSE IPO application status page at https://www.bseindia.com/investors/appli_check
2. Select 'Equity' as the issue type.
3. Choose Mahanadi Coalfields from the IPO list.
4. Enter your application number or PAN, as requested.
5. Submit the details to view your allotment status.

Check IPO bid details on NSE

Step 1. Visit the NSE IPO bid verification page at https://www.nseindia.in/invest/check-trades-bids-verify-ipo-bids
Step 2. Select the relevant IPO from the issue list.
Step 3. Enter the required application details.
Step 4. Submit the information to verify your bid.
Step 5. Your allotment status will be displayed on the screen.

The IPO opened for subscription on November 19 and closed on November 23. The company fixed the price band at Rs 129 to Rs 136 per equity share, with a face value of Rs 2 per share.

The Rs 8,981.12-crore public issue is entirely an offer for sale (OFS) by promoter Coal India, which is selling approximately 66.18 crore equity shares, representing 10 percent of Mahanadi Coalfields' paid-up equity capital.

Since the IPO comprises only an OFS, Mahanadi Coalfields will not receive any proceeds from the offering. The money raised, excluding offer-related expenses, will go to Coal India.

At the upper end of the price band, the company is valued at approximately Rs 90,009.7 crore.

The company has reserved up to 3.31 crore equity shares, or 5 percent of the offer, for eligible employees. These investors are entitled to a discount of Rs 6 per share on the final offer price.

Check IPO News Here

Additionally, 6.61 crore equity shares, representing 10 percent of the offer, have been reserved for eligible shareholders of Coal India.

The basis of allotment is scheduled for November 25. Refunds for unsuccessful applicants and credit of shares to successful applicants' demat accounts are expected on November 26. Mahanadi Coalfields shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on November 27.

SBI Capital Markets, Axis Capital, BOB Capital Markets, IDBI Capital Markets &amp; Securities and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers to the issue. KFin Technologies is the registrar.

About Mahanadi Coalfields

Incorporated in 1992, Mahanadi Coalfields is a Miniratna Category-I public sector enterprise and a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India. Headquartered in Sambalpur, Odisha, the company primarily operates in the Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields.

It is the largest coal-producing subsidiary of Coal India. According to its Red Herring Prospectus, Mahanadi Coalfields produced 218.31 million tonnes of raw coal in FY26, accounting for 28.4 percent of Coal India's total production and around 21 percent of India's domestic coal production.
